newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia lumber talks enter crucial phase.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia lumber talks enter crucial phase.

text.p: Contract negotiations between lumber workers and forestry companies in British Columbia are nearing a crucial stage and a deal or strike vote may come as early as next week, the union said Thursday.
The IWA-Canada was due later Thursday to present a contract proposal to the companies' negotiating body, Forest Industrial Relations, union spokesman Norm Garcia said.
The heads of the companies that belong to Forest Industrial Relations will meet Monday to discuss the proposal. The union hopes an accord will soon follow.
"I think we've gone as far as we can go. It's make or break time," Garcia said.
In the absence of a contract, a strike vote has become "highly possible," he said.
Negotiators have recently been upbeat about progress in negotiations. They have been exchanging contract proposals and meeting since May. Their current contract expired June 14.
The talks cover about 29,000 workers at 65 coastal forestry companies. The coastal contract acts as a benchmark for workers in other regions of the province.
